Latin word

rogō

rogō, rogāre, rogāvī, rogātum

verb, first conjugation; aliquem aliquid rogāre, the person and the thing both in the accusative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

ask (a question, or for something); ask (someone to do something)

In this lexicon

  • ask

    also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 5.1.70: aliud tē rogō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 93; Traupman 28: aliquem aliquid rogāre, to ask someone something; ab aliquō aliquid rogāre, to ask someone for something; dē aliquō rogāre, to ask about

  • request

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.44.1: idque ut faciās vehementer tē rogō

  • rogō ut vōbīs suāviter sit: comfortable

    modern

  • quod rogō: question

    classical

Examples

  • aliud tē rogō

    that’s not what I’m asking youPlaut. Most. 5.1.70 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for ask

  • hoc mihi grātius facere nihil potes, idque ut faciās vehementer tē rogō.

    You can do nothing that would please me more, and I earnestly ask you to do it.Cic. Fam. 13.44.1

    In the entry for request
